content.thinking:
I should note my assumptions clearly: no direct user counts were measured, the deploy event wasn't the cause (the flag was), and I'm using error rate as a proxy for affected account-page requests. I want the executive summary to avoid naming internal components, and I'm drafting the root cause around how enabling the monthly-spend-feature flag exposed a problematic code path in spend_summary.py.

Now I'm working out the full picture: the rollout started partial at 17:35 and hit full traffic at 17:36 with no deploy involved, and only about a third of requests actually failed, suggesting only some accounts triggered the failing condition. I want to flag that the recovery timing correlates with the flag revert, that baseline ClientDisconnected errors are pre-existing and unrelated, and that the exact zero-spend trigger condition is unconfirmed pending review of draft PR #42.

assumptions: Impact is assumed to be confined to account page requests: that is what the error logs show, but per-endpoint impact was not measured separately.
The number of distinct shoppers affected was not measured — only the share of traffic that failed is known.
Recovery is attributed to switching the flag off based on timing (the service returned to baseline right after the revert); no other change was ruled out by experiment.
The pre-incident error level consisted of client-disconnect errors, which are assumed to be normal background noise and unrelated to this fault.
One production change event was found in the 70 minutes before the alert; it was not implicated and is assumed not to have contributed.

The feature was evaluated 'on' for effectively all traffic from 17:36, yet only about a third of requests failed. The specific data condition that triggers the division by zero was not identified; it is assumed only some accounts meet it.
The proposed fix (draft PR #42) is assumed to address the defect but has not been reviewed or verified.
input.executive_summary: On 26 September 2026, a newly enabled feature on the shop's account pages caused a substantial share of account page requests to fail. The fault began at 17:35 UTC and the service was back to its normal error level by 17:41 UTC. Affected shoppers would have seen the account page fail to load; retrying would not reliably have helped while the feature was on, and nothing outside the account page area was implicated. The failure was traced to the newly switched-on feature rather than to any code release, the feature was switched back off, and the service recovered immediately afterwards. A draft code fix has been raised for the underlying defect so the feature can be re-enabled safely.
input.root_cause: Turning on the `monthly-spend-feature` flag (partial rollout at 17:35, fully on by 17:36) routed account page requests through a spend-summary code path that raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, so a large share of those requests returned errors. No code was deployed and no upstream dependency was implicated — the flag flip alone moved the error rate, and turning the flag back off returned the service to baseline.
